newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's likely credit rating Ba3 - HSBC Markets.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's likely credit rating Ba3 - HSBC Markets.

text.p: Vietnam would probably be given a credit rating of Ba3, the same as given to Jordan, Kazakhstan, Romania and Turkey, HSBC Markets said in a report released on Tuesday.

"Given this...spectrum of mid-range ratings from the high of Ba1/BB+ to B2/B, we believe Vietnam will likely fall in the middle at the Ba3 level," HSBC Markets' Senior Country Analyst, David Seto, said in a presentation of his report at the central bank on Monday.
A Moody's Investors Service rating of Ba3 would be equivalent to a Standard & Poor's rating of BB-.

Seto said Vietnam, which is planning to tap the international capital markets soon, had a stable political climate, improving credit measures, powerful growth with falling inflation and strong investor sentiment.
However, while there has been a dramatic rise in the country's savings rate -- to 17.5 percent in 1996 from 13.2 percent in 1991 -- investment has grown even faster.

"The resulting rise of the current account deficit, reaching $2.85 billion in 1996 or 11.6 percent of GDP, is worrisome," he said, noting that there had been a rise in consumer goods imports and short-term debt had increasingly been used to fund imports.
"This type of development is clearly not sustainable in the medium term, given its potential threat to the country's balance of payments," Seto said.
